title: fix(components): render a producer-marked refusal message in the console form
body:
Fixes #5210

An application's hook guards could not talk to their users. When a hook refused a write with 403, the console form replaced the server's text with a generic `form.noPermissionToSave` — the recorded objectstack#3821 remedy, which exists because a raw refusal body puts untranslated platform diagnostics (`FORBIDDEN: insufficient privileges to update showcase_private_note pi-TgoJ4_DM55Fqz`) in front of end users. The external report behind this card (@baozhoutao, against `17.0.0-rc.5`) had **11 hook guards** whose deliberate, localized guidance never reached anyone, and named the incentive that creates: returning 400 instead of 403 for permission failures, degrading the status semantics logs, monitoring and API consumers depend on.

The maintainer ruling (2026-08-19) chose a producer-side opt-in over a chattier 403 branch. The platform half shipped as objectstack#9934: a hook marks its refusal text with `userMessage` at throw time. **This is the consumer half.**

## Pin measurement (the rule-2 obligation, done before the claim)

| reading | measurement |
|:--|:--|
| objectui's pin | `pnpm-lock.yaml` on `origin/main` resolves **one** version of `@objectstack/spec` — `17.2.0` (31 importers, all `specifier: ^17.0.0` → `version: 17.2.0`) |
| that version is published | `registry.npmjs.org/@objectstack/spec` `dist-tags.latest` = `17.2.0` |
| the published tarball carries the marking | `spec-17.2.0.tgz` unpacked: `src/api/contract.zod.ts` and `src/api/errors.zod.ts` both declare `userMessage: z.string().optional()`; `dist/errors.zod-B_A1-ODX.d.ts:317` carries `userMessage: z.ZodOptional<z.ZodString>` |
| the published CHANGELOG records it | `CHANGELOG.md:2277` — *"a hook refusal can mark its message user-facing — `userMessage`, the producer-side opt-in channel (#9934, producer half of objectui#5210)"*, listed under `## 17.1.0` |
| the installed client carries it | `@objectstack/client@17.2.0` `dist/index.js:4347` lifts the field off **both** wire dialects (`body.userMessage`, `body.error.userMessage`) onto `error.userMessage`, verbatim |

**No divergence window** — the pin (`17.2.0`) is ahead of the shipping version (`17.1.0`) and is the current npm `latest`. Nothing here waits on a spec release.

## The marking's shape, read off the installed declaration

Not a remembered key name. Three properties from `ApiErrorSchema.userMessage`'s own doc, and each one decides something in this diff:

- **Presence IS the marking** — *"a field carrying the text, not a boolean beside `message`"*, so no boundary that rewraps or substitutes `message` can promote platform prose into the marked channel, and platform/driver code never sets it.
- **Status-agnostic** — *"Not a 403 special case: any refusal status may carry it."* 403 is where this was reported, not a fence the contract draws.
- **Verbatim** — the author already localized it; none of `extractWriteErrorMessage`'s prefix stripping applies.

The key name is bound to the spec in two independent ways, because either alone is weak: `Pick<ApiError, 'userMessage'>` types the reader at **compile time** (a rename upstream stops compiling), and a pin test asserts the same name at **runtime** against `ApiErrorSchema.shape` — a type-only check is satisfied by a stale `.d.ts`, this one is not.

## What changed

- **`@object-ui/react`** gains `declaredUserMessage(err)` — the one "is this marked?" read. Non-empty string, returned untouched, from the two places the adapter boundary parks the envelope under the same declared key: the error itself and `details` (the identical pair `isPermissionError` reads `code` from). Deliberately **not** read: the raw JSON tail `ApiDataSource` bakes into its message string — scraping a marking out of a transport's prose is the consumer-side guessing objectstack#3821 exists to prevent, and there is a pinned arm asserting it returns `null` for exactly that.
- **`@object-ui/components`** — the form prefers a marked message over both of its generic strings.

## Unmarked messages still get the generic string

Stated plainly because it is the whole safety argument: **a 403 with no marking is byte-identically unchanged** — it still shows `form.noPermissionToSave`, and the raw server text still goes to the browser console only. objectstack#3821's protection is preserved *by construction*, not by re-guessing which 403 bodies are presentable: the mark and the marked text are one field, so this reader can never return text the producer did not opt in. Two of the arms below are controls that exist to keep it that way.

## Verification

All readings taken on `184436b15`, the final commit on this branch, with a clean tree.

**Three arms, each with its control** (`packages/components/src/__tests__/form-write-error-message.test.tsx`):

| arm | asserts |
|:--|:--|
| marked 403 | the author's text renders verbatim; `permission to save` is absent |
| marked 403, leak control | the machine name, the record id and the `FORBIDDEN` prefix stay out of the UI — the marking is additive, not a chattier 403 |
| **CONTROL** — unmarked 403 | generic `form.noPermissionToSave`, unchanged (#3821 not reverted) |
| marked **409** | renders — the marking is status-agnostic |
| **CONTROL** — unmarked non-403 | server message still shown, path unchanged |

```
pnpm vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/react/src/utils/error-message.test.ts \
                               packages/components/src/__tests__/form-write-error-message.test.tsx
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  33 passed (33)
os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0
```

**Reverse verification — two ablations, both predicted before running, both restored.** Neither needed a rebuild, and that is measured rather than assumed: `vitest.config.mts` aliases `@object-ui/react` to `packages/react/src`, so the run reads source, not `dist/`. Each mutation was confirmed **on disk** by grepping the injected marker and the removed text — never an editor exit code — and each script carried a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` restore.

| ablation | predicted | observed |
|:--|:--|:--|
| drop the form's `declaredUserMessage(error) ??` preference | 3 form arms red, both form controls + all 9 reader arms green | `Tests 3 failed \| 30 passed` — exactly the three marked arms |
| make the reader return `null` unconditionally | 4 reader arms + 3 form arms red; the `null`-asserting arms green | `Tests 7 failed \| 26 passed` — exactly those seven |

On-disk proof, ablation 1: `removed text 'declaredUserMessage(error) ??' occurrences: 0` / `injected marker 'ABLATED-5210' occurrences: 1`. After restore: `git diff HEAD --stat` empty, marker count `0`, original text count `1`, green re-run `33 passed (33)`.

**Legs that do not discriminate**, named rather than counted as evidence: the two form CONTROL arms and the five `null`-asserting reader arms stay green under both ablations — by design, they pin the #3821 behaviour that must *not* move.

**Gates** — each exit code captured before any pipe, each verdict quoted from the gate's own output:

```
check-changeset-presence      EXIT=0  ✅ 5 source file(s) of 2 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)
check-changeset-no-major      EXIT=0  ✅ No changeset declares a `major` bump.
check-control-bytes           EXIT=0  ✅ OK (scanned 4909 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary)
check-phantom-dependencies    EXIT=0  ✅ Every in-scope import is declared by the package that publishes it.
check-spec-symbol-derivation  EXIT=0  ✅ 1300 files scanned against 4959 spec export names
check-i18n-call-site-keys     EXIT=0  Every in-scope call-site key resolves against the en pack (2929 keys)
check-i18n-en-drift           EXIT=0  No en value changed in this range.
check-lint-coverage           EXIT=0  ✅ 46/46 packages linted, 0 with outstanding errors
check-type-check-coverage     EXIT=0  ✅ 45/46 via `type-check`, 0 errors outstanding
```

No locale key was added or changed — the i18n gates are run because the touched file calls `t()`, not because this diff moves a pack.

**Type-check**, script name echoed so a zero-match filter cannot read as green:

```
packages/react type-check$ tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json      → Done
packages/components type-check$ tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json → Done
os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0
```

**Lint — no narrowing to declare for the touched packages.** `pnpm --filter @object-ui/react --filter @object-ui/components lint` runs the same per-package `eslint .` CI runs, over both packages whole:

```
packages/react lint$ eslint .        → ✖ 354 problems (0 errors, 354 warnings)
packages/components lint$ eslint .   → ✖ 906 problems (0 errors, 906 warnings)
```

**0 errors** in both; every warning is pre-existing. Measured, not asserted: intersecting eslint's `--format json` output with the line ranges this commit adds gives **0 messages on any added line** (5 files, 239 added lines). The other 44 packages were not linted here, and cannot be affected — ESLint's own resolution reports `parserOptions.project: null` and `projectService: null` for the touched files, so linting is not type-aware and a file's verdict depends only on its own text plus the shared config, neither of which this diff moves for an untouched file.

## Findings filed alongside, not fixed here

Both unassigned, `finding` + `domain:ui`, after a duplicate scan over all 220 open issues:

- #5901 — `normaliseClientError` drops the marking when it re-wraps `VALIDATION_FAILED` / `CONCURRENT_UPDATE`; the 403 path this PR serves passes through unchanged (probe measured both, then deleted uncommitted).
- #5902 — the kanban and calendar drag-write surfaces still substitute a generic string for a marked refusal.

Left out on purpose: both sit in other packages with their own suites, and the ruling this PR implements names the console form. #5901 and #5902 remain open.
